big: The 50-day line crosses above the 200-day line. Some call it a golden cross. Indicators turn price history into simple signals, but they describe the past and can mislead. Education, not a call to trade.

lines: The average price over a set number of days, updated daily to smooth out noise. A 200-day line shows long-term direction. A golden cross is a short average rising above a long one. MACD uses the gap between a fast and a slow average. A trendline joins lows or highs.

q: A 200-day line shows the long-term direction of a share. What is it?
why: A candlestick is one period's open, high, low, close.
A volume bar counts shares traded. The details here point elsewhere.
A target price is a forecast. That does not match this case.
It is the average price over 200 days. That matches the case described.

q: The 50-day line crosses above the 200-day line. What is this called?
why: Head and shoulders is a peak pattern. The details here point elsewhere.
A short average rising above a long one is a golden cross.
A breakdown is a fall through support. It does not fit the facts given.
A margin call is a futures demand. It does not answer what was asked.

q: A line built from a 12-day and a 26-day average crosses its signal line. Which indicator is this?
why: MACD is based on fast and slow averages. That matches the case described.
RSI is a momentum indicator. It does not answer what was asked.
VWAP is a volume-weighted price. The details here point elsewhere.
PEG is a valuation ratio. The details here point elsewhere.

q: A line joining the last four higher lows slopes upwards. What is this?
why: A candlestick is one period's bar.
A trendline is drawn along lows or highs.
A hurdle rate is a return threshold.

pts: Moving average: average price over a set number of days.
Golden cross: a short average above a long one. MACD: gap between fast and slow averages.
A trendline joins lows or highs. Signals can fail.
